narr: An active period of weather produced Isolated strong to severe storms on the 9th. Residual boundaries from these storms combined with the remnants of an MCS during the afternoon of the 10th which produced strong to severe storms with heavy rainfall|during the late afternoon and early evening. Instability remained high and precipitable water had increased to nearly two inches. Reports of straight line wind damage were received from Nixa in Christian County eastward into Douglas, Wright, Texas and Howell Counties. In Webster County, several locations received between two and a half inches and five inches of rain.
ev: Highway W was flooded and impassable north of Highway EE and at Hawk Pond Branch.
State Highway W was flooded and impassable at Givens Branch.
Highway Y was flooded and impassable at the Niangua River.
lsr: ABOUT 10 INCHES OF WATER FLOWING OVER HIGHWAY W ABOUT A MILE NORTH OF STATE HIGHWAY EE. WATER WAS ALSO OVER THE ROADWAY AT HAWK POND BRANCH AND HIGHWAY W.
WATER FLOWING OVER STATE HIGHWAY W AT GIVINS BRANCH. UNKNOWN DEPTH.
